description:
Suppliers become a first-class domain linkable to brands, and products gain the category column that unblocks W6.

Epic: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md (Epic 3)
Architecture: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md
Requires: W1 merged into august-6th-updates in both repos
Blocks: W6 (needs products.category)

userStories.title: Migration: suppliers, aliases and the two FK columns
userStories.description: As the platform, I want a canonical supplier record, so that a house can be linked to who invoices it.
acceptanceCriteria: suppliers has a unique name and slug, a d365_token, and archived_at with a partial live index
currency is the supplier INVOICING currency, not the country default — Jim Thompson is Thailand but USD
supplier_aliases is unique on lower(btrim(alias))
brands.supplier_id references suppliers ON DELETE RESTRICT
price_list_items.supplier_id references suppliers ON DELETE SET NULL, beside the retained free-text supplier
NO cost column is added to brands — brand rows are served to anonymous visitors
Re-running the migration is a no-op
Gates green: `( cd atelier-api && npm run lint && npm test )`

userStories.title: Migration: supplier brand terms and discount tiers
userStories.description: As the office, I want per-brand commercial terms recorded where they cannot leak.
acceptanceCriteria: supplier_brand_terms holds discount, discount_chain (array) and markup, unique per brand
A test proves a {0.4, 0.4} chain evaluates to x0.36, not -80%
Terms tables are never joined into any client-facing read model
Gates green: `( cd atelier-api && npm run lint && npm test )`

userStories.title: Migration: products.category
userStories.description: As the office, I want products categorised on the same axis as supplier rates, so that the catalogue and the rate ledger are joinable.
acceptanceCriteria: category is text with CHECK (category IN ('fabric','wallpaper','trimming','accessory'))
It is nullable — existing products are uncategorised, not wrong
It matches price_list_items.category exactly
Gates green: `( cd atelier-api && npm run lint && npm test )`

userStories.title: Supplier read models and admin module
userStories.description: As the CRM, I want to list and read suppliers.
acceptanceCriteria: List supports q, include_archived and pagination
The column whitelist is frozen and in-code, as buildUpdate requires
Cost-bearing fields are present here (this is back-office only) but a test asserts they never appear in any /catalogue/* response
Gates green: `( cd atelier-api && npm run lint && npm test )`

userStories.title: Supplier routes including DELETE
userStories.description: As back-office staff, I want to manage suppliers and be told when one cannot be removed.
acceptanceCriteria: requireRole backoffice on every route
DELETE is blocked by brands and price_list_items, each with a count
brands.supplier_id is RESTRICT, so the 23503 backstop is exercised by a test
Duplicate name returns 409 from the database, never a pre-check
Gates green: `( cd atelier-api && npm run lint && npm test )`

userStories.title: Backfill suppliers from existing data
userStories.description: As the office, I want the supplier list populated from what we already hold, so that nobody retypes 40 names.
acceptanceCriteria: Sources: SELECT DISTINCT price_list_items.supplier and src/seed/data/suppliers.js
SUPPLIER_OVERRIDES (JV, JWall, C&C) become supplier_aliases rows
price_list_items.supplier_id is populated by matching name then alias
Rows that cannot be matched are reported, not guessed
Re-running changes nothing
Gates green: `( cd atelier-api && npm run lint && npm test )`

userStories.title: AdminSuppliers CRM screen
userStories.description: As back-office staff, I want to manage suppliers in the CRM.
acceptanceCriteria: Uses useAdminList, Pagination and useCrudScreen from W1
The existing demo Suppliers screen is untouched and reachable via a suppliersTabs strip
Cost fields respect CAPS.FINANCE_VIEW masking
Gates green: `( cd atelier-crm && npm test && npm run build )`
